papers.title: Dataset Distillation for Pre-Trained Self-Supervised Vision Models
papers.abstract: The task of dataset distillation aims to find a small set of synthetic images such that training a model on them reproduces the performance of the same model trained on a much larger dataset of real samples. Existing distillation methods focus on synthesizing datasets that enable training randomly initialized models. In contrast, state-of-the-art vision approaches are increasingly building on large, pre-trained self-supervised models rather than training from scratch. In this paper, we investigate the problem of distilling datasets that enable us to optimally train linear probes on top of such large, pre-trained vision models. We introduce a method of dataset distillation for this task called Linear Gradient Matching that optimizes the synthetic images such that, when passed through a pre-trained feature extractor, they induce gradients in the linear classifier similar to those produced by the real data. Our method yields synthetic data that outperform all real-image baselines and, remarkably, generalize across pre-trained vision models, enabling us, for instance, to train a linear CLIP probe that performs competitively using a dataset distilled via a DINO backbone. Further, we show that our distilled datasets are exceptionally effective for fine-grained classification and provide a valuable tool for model interpretability, predicting, among other things, how similar two models' embedding spaces are under the platonic representation hypothesis or whether a model is sensitive to spurious correlations in adversarial datasets.

# Dataset Distillation for Pre-Trained Self-Supervised Vision Models: Research Analysis

## Comprehensive Summary

This groundbreaking research addresses a critical challenge in machine learning: dataset distillation for pre-trained self-supervised vision models. Unlike previous approaches that focused on synthesizing datasets for models trained from scratch, this study introduces a novel method called Linear Gradient Matching that targets optimizing synthetic images for linear probes on large, pre-trained vision models.

The research fundamentally shifts the paradigm of dataset creation by demonstrating that synthetic datasets can not only match but potentially outperform real-image datasets when used with pre-trained models. By carefully constructing synthetic images that induce similar gradient behaviors to real training data, the authors show the potential for more efficient and interpretable machine learning techniques.

The work has significant implications for model efficiency, interpretability, and transfer learning, offering a sophisticated approach to creating compact, high-performance datasets that can generalize across different pre-trained vision model architectures.

## Key Findings

### Methodological Innovations
- Introduced **Linear Gradient Matching** as a novel dataset distillation technique
- Successfully created synthetic datasets that outperform real-image baselines
- Demonstrated cross-model generalizability of distilled datasets

### Performance Highlights
- Achieved competitive linear probe performance using distilled datasets
- Showed effectiveness in fine-grained classification tasks
- Enabled advanced model interpretability techniques

### Theoretical Contributions
- Validated the potential of synthetic datasets for pre-trained models
- Provided insights into embedding space similarities
- Demonstrated a method for detecting model sensitivity to spurious correlations

### Practical Implications
- Reduced computational and data requirements for model training
- Offered a new approach to understanding and comparing vision models
- Created a framework for more efficient machine learning workflows

## Technical Significance
The research represents a significant step forward in dataset synthesis, bridging the gap between traditional training approaches and modern pre-trained self-supervised models. By focusing on gradient matching rather than direct performance replication, the method offers a more nuanced and potentially more generalizable approach to dataset distillation.

papers.title: EvoLMM: Self-Evolving Large Multimodal Models with Continuous Rewards
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large multimodal models (LMMs) have enabled impressive reasoning and perception abilities, yet most existing training pipelines still depend on human-curated data or externally verified reward models, limiting their autonomy and scalability. In this work, we strive to improve LMM reasoning capabilities in a purely unsupervised fashion (without any annotated data or reward distillation). To this end, we propose a self-evolving framework, named EvoLMM, that instantiates two cooperative agents from a single backbone model: a Proposer, which generates diverse, image-grounded questions, and a Solver, which solves them through internal consistency, where learning proceeds through a continuous self-rewarding process. This dynamic feedback encourages both the generation of informative queries and the refinement of structured reasoning without relying on ground-truth or human judgments. When using the popular Qwen2.5-VL as the base model, our EvoLMM yields consistent gains upto $\sim$3\% on multimodal math-reasoning benchmarks, including ChartQA, MathVista, and MathVision, using only raw training images. We hope our simple yet effective approach will serve as a solid baseline easing future research in self-improving LMMs in a fully-unsupervised fashion. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/EvoLMM.
papers.summary:
# EvoLMM: Self-Evolving Large Multimodal Models with Continuous Rewards

## Comprehensive Summary

The research introduces EvoLMM, an innovative self-evolving framework designed to enhance large multimodal models' (LMMs) reasoning capabilities through an autonomous, unsupervised learning approach. Unlike traditional methods that rely on human-curated data or external reward models, EvoLMM creates a self-improving mechanism by splitting a single backbone model into two cooperative agents: a Proposer and a Solver.

The Proposer generates diverse, image-grounded questions, while the Solver attempts to solve these queries through internal consistency. This unique approach enables continuous self-rewarding and learning without dependence on ground-truth annotations or human judgments. By leveraging this dynamic feedback loop, the framework aims to simultaneously improve query generation quality and reasoning structure, ultimately advancing multimodal model performance.

Experimental validation using the Qwen2.5-VL base model demonstrates the framework's effectiveness, achieving consistent performance gains of approximately 3% across challenging multimodal math-reasoning benchmarks like ChartQA, MathVista, and MathVision, using only raw training images.

## Key Findings

### Methodological Innovations
- Introduced a novel self-evolving framework for unsupervised LMM training
- Created a two-agent system (Proposer and Solver) within a single backbone model
- Implemented a continuous self-rewarding process without external annotations

### Performance Highlights
- Achieved ~3% performance improvement on math-reasoning benchmarks
- Demonstrated effectiveness using raw training images
- Showed consistent gains across multiple multimodal reasoning datasets

### Theoretical Contributions
- Proposed a framework for autonomous model improvement
- Reduced dependency on human-curated data and external reward models
- Established a baseline for self-improving large multimodal models

### Practical Implications
- Opened new research directions in unsupervised multimodal model training
- Provided a flexible approach adaptable to different base models
- Simplified the model enhancement process through internal consistency

## Potential Impact
The research represents a significant step towards more autonomous and self-improving artificial intelligence systems, particularly in the domain of multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: Thinking-while-Generating: Interleaving Textual Reasoning throughout Visual Generation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in visual generation have increasingly explored the integration of reasoning capabilities. They incorporate textual reasoning, i.e., think, either before (as pre-planning) or after (as post-refinement) the generation process, yet they lack on-the-fly multimodal interaction during the generation itself. In this preliminary study, we introduce Thinking-while-Generating (TwiG), the first interleaved framework that enables co-evolving textual reasoning throughout the visual generation process. As visual content is progressively generating, textual reasoning is interleaved to both guide upcoming local regions and reflect on previously synthesized ones. This dynamic interplay produces more context-aware and semantically rich visual outputs. To unveil the potential of this framework, we investigate three candidate strategies, zero-shot prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on our curated TwiG-50K dataset, and reinforcement learning (RL) via a customized TwiG-GRPO strategy, each offering unique insights into the dynamics of interleaved reasoning. We hope this work inspires further research into interleaving textual reasoning for enhanced visual generation. Code will be released at: https://github.com/ZiyuGuo99/Thinking-while-Generating.
papers.summary:
# Research Paper Analysis: Thinking-while-Generating (TwiG)

## Comprehensive Summary

The research introduces Thinking-while-Generating (TwiG), an innovative framework that fundamentally reimagines visual generation by integrating textual reasoning dynamically throughout the generation process. Unlike existing approaches that treat reasoning as a pre-planning or post-refinement step, TwiG enables a continuous, co-evolutionary interaction between textual reasoning and visual content generation. This approach allows for real-time guidance and reflection, potentially producing more contextually rich and semantically nuanced visual outputs.

The study explores three distinct strategies for implementing this interleaved reasoning approach: zero-shot prompting, supervised fine-tuning using a custom TwiG-50K dataset, and a novel reinforcement learning method called TwiG-GRPO. By investigating these approaches, the researchers aim to demonstrate the potential of simultaneous, ongoing reasoning during the visual generation process, challenging traditional sequential generation paradigms.

## Key Findings

### Methodological Innovations
- First framework to integrate textual reasoning *during* visual generation
- Introduces dynamic, interleaved reasoning approach
- Enables real-time semantic guidance and reflection

### Strategy Exploration
- Tested three reasoning strategies:
  * Zero-shot prompting
  * Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
  * Reinforcement learning (RL via TwiG-GRPO)

### Potential Contributions
- Enhanced context-awareness in visual generation
- More semantically rich visual outputs
- Demonstrates potential for multimodal interaction during generation

### Technical Significance
- Challenges traditional sequential generation models
- Proposes a novel approach to incorporating reasoning in generative AI
- Opens new research directions in multimodal AI generation

## Scholarly Assessment
This preliminary study represents a significant conceptual advancement in visual generation, offering a more dynamic and interactive approach to AI-driven content creation. The research's primary contribution lies in its innovative framework that continuously integrates reasoning throughout the generation process.

papers.title: Strained hyperbolic Dirac fermions: Zero modes, flat bands, and competing orders
papers.abstract: Starting from the nearest-neighbor tight-binding model on {10,3} and {14,3} hyperbolic lattices that, for a uniform hopping amplitude, gives rise to emergent Dirac fermions on a curved space with a constant negative curvature, displaying a vanishing density of states, we propose spatially modulated hopping pattern therein that preserve the underlying 5- and 7-fold rotational symmetries, respectively, and effectively couples fermions to time-reversal symmetric axial magnetic fields. Such strain-induced axial fields produce a flat band near zero-energy, triggering nucleation of a charge density-wave, featuring a staggered pattern of fermionic density between two sublattices, and the Haldane phase fostering intra-sublattice circulating currents with a net zero magnetic flux for weak nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor Coulomb repulsions, respectively. Sufficiently weak on-site Hubbard repulsion destabilizes such flat bands toward the formation of a magnetic phase that simultaneously supports antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic orders in the whole system. While the magnetization in the bulk and boundary cancel each other, the Neél order is of the same sign everywhere, thereby yielding a global antiferromagnet. Throughout, we draw parallels between these findings and the well-studied qualitatively similar results on a 3-fold rotational symmetric strained honeycomb lattice, thereby unifying the phenomenon of axial magnetic catalysis for Dirac fermions, encompassing the ones living on the Euclidean plane. Finally, we show that with a specific class of non-Hermiticity, manifesting via an imbalance in the hopping amplitudes between two sublattices in the opposite directions, magnitudes of all these orders can be boosted substantially when all the eigenvalues in the noninteracting systems are real, staging a non-Hermitian amplification of axial magnetic catalysis.

# Research Paper Analysis: Strained Hyperbolic Dirac Fermions

## Concise Summary

This research explores the fascinating quantum mechanical behavior of Dirac fermions on hyperbolic lattices with spatially modulated hopping patterns. The authors investigate how strain-induced axial magnetic fields can dramatically alter the electronic structure of these complex geometric systems, revealing emergent quantum phases with unique electronic and magnetic properties.

The study focuses on {10,3} and {14,3} hyperbolic lattices, demonstrating how carefully designed hopping patterns can create exotic quantum states. By introducing spatially modulated hopping that preserves rotational symmetries, the researchers uncover mechanisms for generating flat bands, charge density waves, and intriguing magnetic phases that challenge conventional understanding of electronic behavior in curved geometric spaces.

## Key Findings

### Quantum Structural Discoveries
- Emergence of zero-energy density of states in hyperbolic lattices
- Creation of flat bands through strain-induced axial magnetic fields
- Preservation of 5- and 7-fold rotational symmetries in the lattice

### Electronic Phase Transitions
- Charge density wave formation with staggered fermionic density
- Haldane phase supporting intra-sublattice circulating currents
- Magnetic phase supporting simultaneous antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic orders

### Unique Quantum Phenomena
- Magnetization that cancels in bulk and boundary
- Global antiferromagnetic order with consistent Néel sign
- Non-Hermitian amplification of axial magnetic catalysis

### Methodological Innovation
- Utilized nearest-neighbor tight-binding model on hyperbolic lattices
- Introduced spatially modulated hopping patterns
- Examined effects of weak Coulomb and Hubbard repulsions

## Significance
The research provides a comprehensive framework for understanding quantum behavior in curved geometric spaces, bridging theoretical insights across different lattice configurations and opening new avenues for exploring exotic quantum states.

papers.title: Nemotron Elastic: Towards Efficient Many-in-One Reasoning LLMs
papers.abstract: Training a family of large language models targeting multiple scales and deployment objectives is prohibitively expensive, requiring separate training runs for each different size. Recent work on model compression through pruning and knowledge distillation has reduced this cost; however, this process still incurs hundreds of billions of tokens worth of training cost per compressed model. In this paper, we present Nemotron Elastic, a framework for building reasoning-oriented LLMs, including hybrid Mamba-Attention architectures, that embed multiple nested submodels within a single parent model, each optimized for different deployment configurations and budgets. Each of these submodels shares weights with the parent model and can be extracted zero-shot during deployment without additional training or fine-tuning. We enable this functionality through an end-to-end trained router, tightly coupled to a two-stage training curriculum designed specifically for reasoning models. We additionally introduce group-aware SSM elastification that preserves Mamba's structural constraints, heterogeneous MLP elastification, normalized MSE-based layer importance for improved depth selection, and knowledge distillation enabling simultaneous multi-budget optimization. We apply Nemotron Elastic to the Nemotron Nano V2 12B model, simultaneously producing a 9B and a 6B model using only 110B training tokens; this results in over 360x cost reduction compared to training model families from scratch, and around 7x compared to SoTA compression techniques. Each of the nested models performs on par or better than the SoTA in accuracy. Moreover, unlike other compression methods, the nested capability of our approach allows having a many-in-one reasoning model that has constant deployment memory against the number of models in the family.
papers.summary:
# Nemotron Elastic: Research Paper Analysis

## Concise Summary

Nemotron Elastic introduces a groundbreaking framework for efficiently creating multiple large language models (LLMs) within a single parent model. The research addresses the significant computational and financial challenges of training separate models for different scales and deployment configurations by developing an innovative approach that enables embedded, zero-shot extractable submodels.

The core innovation lies in an end-to-end trained router mechanism coupled with a specialized two-stage training curriculum focused on reasoning capabilities. By implementing techniques like group-aware SSM elastification and heterogeneous MLP elastification, the researchers demonstrate the ability to generate multiple model sizes simultaneously using minimal training resources. This approach represents a substantial leap in model compression and efficiency, dramatically reducing the computational cost of developing model families.

## Key Findings

### Computational Efficiency
- Achieved over **360x cost reduction** compared to training model families from scratch
- Approximately **7x more efficient** than state-of-the-art compression techniques
- Generated 9B and 6B models using only 110B training tokens

### Technical Innovations
- Developed a router-based framework for nested submodel extraction
- Introduced group-aware SSM elastification preserving Mamba's architectural constraints
- Implemented heterogeneous MLP elastification
- Created normalized MSE-based layer importance for depth selection

### Performance Outcomes
- Demonstrated equivalent or superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art models
- Achieved constant deployment memory regardless of model family size
- Enabled zero-shot submodel extraction without additional training

### Unique Capabilities
- Supports hybrid Mamba-Attention architectures
- Enables multiple model sizes within a single training process
- Provides flexible deployment configurations

## Significance
This research represents a significant advancement in large language model development, addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency and model flexibility.

# AI Agents in Healthcare: Research Landscape Synthesis

## 1. Executive Summary

The emerging landscape of AI agents in healthcare represents a transformative convergence of advanced machine learning techniques, multimodal reasoning, and innovative computational approaches. Across the reviewed research, a clear trend emerges: AI systems are progressively moving beyond traditional task-specific implementations towards more dynamic, self-evolving, and contextually intelligent frameworks.

The research demonstrates a significant shift towards more autonomous, adaptable AI agents capable of continuous learning, nuanced reasoning, and complex multimodal interactions. Key innovations include self-evolving models (EvoLMM), dynamic reasoning during generation (Thinking-while-Generating), and efficient model architectures that can generate multiple model configurations with minimal computational overhead.
